output.impression: Severe executive dysfunction (FAB 11/18, Trails B discontinued, perseverative WCST errors) and impaired social cognition (Faux Pas 4/20, theory of mind failed), with a retrieval-type memory deficit, normal recognition and preserved visuospatial perception. The profile is executive and social-cognitive predominant with relative sparing of memory recognition and visuospatial function, consistent with a frontal-network syndrome.

output.impression: No C9orf72 expansion and no pathogenic GRN or MAPT variant. A negative panel does not exclude frontotemporal lobar degeneration; most people without a family history have no identified variant.

action_criteria.label: Structured informant history and bedside cognitive screen scored against the Rascovsky features
action_criteria.rationale: The diagnosis of bvFTD rests on the behavioural features obtained from an informant; the screen documents the cognitive profile.

action_criteria.label: Reversible-cause blood tests: CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, ESR, CRP
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, endocrine, nutritional and inflammatory contributors before attributing decline to neurodegeneration.

action_criteria.label: MRI brain without contrast, dementia protocol
action_criteria.rationale: Shows the frontal and anterior temporal atrophy pattern and excludes structural and vascular causes.

action_criteria.label: FDG-PET when the structural picture is unresolved
action_criteria.rationale: Frontal and anterior temporal hypometabolism with posterior sparing supports FTD over AD.

action_criteria.rationale: Onset about 60 without a suggestive family history: the FTD consortium advises C9orf72 screening in possible or probable bvFTD, UK eligibility does not, so a counselled panel is optional.

action_criteria.label: Interaction check before an SSRI for disinhibition and compulsive behaviour

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on bvFTD criteria and supportive care
action_criteria.label: Literature search on bvFTD criteria and management
action_criteria.rationale: General background only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD, NICE NG97 advises against it, and it may worsen behaviour.
Do not start memantine: a randomised trial showed no benefit in FTD and NICE NG97 advises against it.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
required_recommendations: Apply the Rascovsky 2011 criteria: state which features are present, the functional decline, and the level of certainty (possible or probable).
Explain why a late-onset primary psychiatric disorder does not account for the progressive syndrome (no psychiatric history, no mood symptoms, frontal release signs and lobar atrophy).

Address safety and capacity: driving, finances (over $8,000 of online gambling: restrict access to accounts and gambling sites), the shoplifting, supervision while she lives alone, and lasting power of attorney while she can still take part.
Arrange caregiver education and support, and a plan for behavioural symptoms that avoids cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not part of the FTD work-up; FDG-PET, or perfusion SPECT where it is unavailable, is the functional study used when needed.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; she has no parkinsonism and it would not change the diagnosis.

accepted: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, sporadic

differential.key_features: Bedside recall, orientation and clock are impaired, but memory is of retrieval type with normal recognition, the hippocampi are normal and the atrophy is orbitofrontal and anterior temporal with posterior sparing; an amyloid or CSF AD biomarker study is optional if doubt remains.

differential.diagnosis: Primary psychiatric disorder (late-onset bipolar disorder, personality change)
differential.key_features: No psychiatric history before 60 and no mood elevation or depressive symptoms; progressive decline, frontal release signs, utilisation behaviour and lobar atrophy indicate a neurodegenerative cause.
Treated hypothyroidism with TSH 1.8 mIU/L on levothyroxine: euthyroid.
No fasciculations, bulbar dysfunction, wasting or limb weakness on examination.

key_clinical_evidence: Three Rascovsky features on her son's account (disinhibition, compulsive arranging, hyperorality), with loss of her post and unsafe finances, meet possible bvFTD with significant functional decline.
Severe right-predominant orbitofrontal and anterior temporal atrophy with a knife-blade pattern, normal hippocampi and preserved posterior cortex on MRI give the imaging support for probable bvFTD.
Neuropsychology shows severe executive and social-cognition deficits with a retrieval-type memory deficit, normal recognition and preserved visuospatial perception.
The frontal and anterior temporal pattern with relative posterior sparing makes Alzheimer disease less likely; an amyloid or CSF AD biomarker study is optional if doubt remains.
Treated hypothyroidism is controlled (TSH 1.8 mIU/L) and does not explain the syndrome.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: TSH 1.8 mIU/L on replacement: she is euthyroid, and hypothyroidism does not produce a disinhibited, compulsive frontal syndrome with lobar atrophy.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Could suggest a hypothyroid contribution to cognitive and behavioural change.

sequence_constraints.reason: Genetic testing follows the clinical diagnosis and counselling.

clinical_assessment.impression: 3 of the 6 Rascovsky features are present on informant history and examination (disinhibition, compulsive behaviour, hyperorality), with documented decline in daily function. This meets possible bvFTD; imaging and neuropsychological testing decide whether it is probable. Memory and visuospatial items are also impaired on the bedside screen, which keeps Alzheimer disease in the differential.

Behavioural variant FTD diagnostic crite.summary: Rascovsky and colleagues (2011) define possible behavioural variant FTD by three of six behavioural and cognitive features, probable bvFTD by added functional decline and frontal or anterior temporal involvement on structural or functional imaging, and definite bvFTD by histopathology or a pathogenic mutation. Psychiatric disorders are the main mimics and are excluded on course and examination rather than on a single test. Treatment is supportive: SSRIs or trazodone for behaviour, caregiver support and safety planning; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are not recommended.

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. V. is a 62-year-old right-handed Hispanic woman referred by her son for progressive personality changes over 2 years. He reports that his mother, formerly a reserved and professional school principal known for her decorum, began making inappropriate remarks at school board meetings approximately 2 years ago. She was eventually asked to retire early. Over the past year, her behavior has escalated markedly. She makes crude sexual jokes to strangers, has been found shoplifting small items (which she denies), and has made repeated unwanted advances toward a neighbor. She has developed compulsive behavior around food — she will eat continuously and has started eating food off other people's plates without permission. She also has a new compulsion to arrange objects in her kitchen in precise patterns for hours. Her son has found evidence of online gambling, spending over $8,000 in six months. She expresses no concern about any of this, stating she is 'finally doing what she wants.' She complains of no depressive symptoms, hallucinations, or pain. Neurological review of systems otherwise negative.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, disinhibited. Uses profanity repeatedly, which son confirms is completely out of character. Asks examiner personal questions about marital status without social filter. Exhibits utilization behavior: turns on examination light unprompted.
